Mate Rimac's Bugatti Got Stolen: He Found the Thief in Austria, Wanted To Give Him a Lift Home
12 photos
Photo: Mate Rimac | Instagram
Bugatti Rimac CEO Mate Rimac had his personal $3.3 million Bugatti Chiron stolen from the company's unfenced campus in Croatia. Rimac made one rookie mistake, overestimating the safety of the campus: he left the keys inside the vehicle and walked into his office. The thief was already on his way to Germany by the time the owner of the car realized it was gone. When he found his car, he wanted to give the man a lift home
A 36-year-old Croatian man wandering the campus looking for a job spotted the Bugatti Chiron parked with the keys inside. Security cameras caught the man finishing a cigarette before hopping in and driving off in broad daylight.
Because factory employees frequently move cars for testing and his Chiron is often driven around the campus by others, Mate Rimac always leaves it with the keys inside. So when he saw it was not parked where he had left it, he just assumed someone needed to move it. However, he was eventually told that a stranger drove off in his Chiron.
At this point, Mate Rimac called the police. Authorities reported the theft to neighboring countries. By that time, the thief and the car had already crossed the border. In the meantime, Mate Rimac did not just sit with his arms crossed, waiting for the police to solve the case. He used the Chiron's built-in advanced telemetry tracking system to pull up real-time live coordinates, speed metrics, and fuel level.
Photo: Mate Rimac | Instagram Once he got access to the real-time location, Rimac and his team set up a digital command center by launching a group chat that included local law enforcement. However, he was not going to just sit in his office and let the police chase the thief.
Mate got in his Porsche 911 Turbo S and started his own chase. He knew that the thief would not get very far with the gas he had left in the tank of the Chiron. He did stop for a refill and, as expected, left without paying. That was when his one-hour head start was reduced, while Rimac was pushing his Porsche to close the gap.
The telemetry showed the thief blazing past the Slovenian border and crossing straight into Austria. Rimac's team kept feeding data to the authorities. The Austrian police coordinated an interception strategy and cornered the thief along the A9 Pyhrn motorway near Graz.
Mate Rimac expected to just flash his ID, thank the officers, and drive his Bugatti back home to Croatia. Instead, he found about 10 police cars and 20 officers at the scene. Because the Chiron had been involved in an international theft and was worth millions, the Austrian police refused to simply hand it over on the side of the road.
Photo: Rimac Automobili Police ordered the Bugatti to be loaded onto a flatbed tow truck and moved to the local police precinct. So the owner had to follow the police caravan to the station and stay there until the early hours of the next morning, filling out international cross-border grand theft paperwork.
It was during this late-night stint at the precinct that Rimac asked to meet the thief face to face. What would have normally been a very heated confrontation turned into a remarkably calm conversation.
He found out that the 36-year-old suspect was coming from a very difficult background and had originally walked into the unfenced Bugatti campus to ask for a job, but when he saw the Chiron and noticed it had the keys in, he just couldn't help himself.
The Bugatti CEO recalled with a bit of amusement that the thief framed it " like it was my faul t" for tempting him with an open car. He confessed that he had no grand black-market smuggling operation plans. He simply panicked, put his foot down, and headed for Germany for completely unknown reasons.
Photo: Mate Rimac | Instagram Rimac explained that he leaves his cars unlocked all the time because Croatia is incredibly safe. Regardless of the country's crime rate, he will probably think twice when he gets out of the car and walks away.
Impressed by the man's story, state of mind, and family situation, Mate Rimac decided not to press charges and said he would have gladly picked the man up and driven him back home to his family himself. However, the case is completely out of his hands. Public prosecutors in Graz, Austria, and the Croatian police are moving forward with criminal prosecution.
The Bugatti Chiron sustained some minor damage to its front end during the multi-country getaway. Rimac brushed it off on social media, saying, " I don't care, we will repair it, " says the man who occaasionally drives a Volkswagen Golf R32 . A new front spoiler for the CEO of a company that builds hypercars is not exactly something to worry about.
Don't be surprised if Mate Rimac calls the man for an interview and hires him at Bugatti. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mate Rimac (@materimac)

Brand-New Amangati to Complete a Spectacular Wellness-Centric Atlantic Passage
10 photos
Photo: Aman At Sea/Instagram
One of the newest and most impressive ships to join the luxury cruise sector is Amangati, the first ship operated by hospitality luxury brand Aman. Amangati’s maiden season, set to debut in 2027, is already available for booking, but one of the most spectacular voyages is announced for the end of 2027 and beginning of 2028.
Aman Group is one of the latest luxury hospitality brand to dive into the world of luxury cruising, expanding their operations from hotels and resorts to sea travel. Aman at Sea, a joint venture between Aman Group and Cruise Saudi, was established in 2023, and it will operate the brand’s first cruise ship, the superb Amangati.
“Aman” means peace in Sanskrit, and “Amangati” translates to “peaceful motion”, a beautiful symbol of the brand’s “peaceful luxury” concept, reflected in every one of the 36 hotels and resorts operated in some of the most breathtaking locations on earth.
Amangati follows the popular industry trend of “superyacht-inspired” cruise ships, either motor yachts or sailing yachts. The idea is to go beyond boutique cruising and offer an onboard experience that’s as close as possible to that of a private superyacht – from enhanced privacy for each guest to pampering comfort and impeccable service.
The 600-foot (183 meters) Amangati will offer no more than 47 suites, for a more intimate onboard experience. Superyacht-inspired amenities include a stunning 16-meter (52.5-foot) swimming pool on Deck 6, spacious suites with full-height windows and spa-like en-suites, plus a generous water toy box coupled with a large beach club, very similar to that of popular charter yachts.
Following the inaugural Mediterranean season planned for mid-2027, Amangati will get ready for a spectacular Winter season comprised of Atlantic Passages centered around wellness. The first 13-night Atlantic Passage from Malaga to Saint John’s will include four port stops. The itinerary is designed to follow the ancient mariners’ route to Cadiz, and the Azore islands, before sailing into the Atlantic.
Prices are steep, with the Deluxe Suites ((703 to 731 square feet) starting at $54,600 per voyage, as the most affordable options onboard. The Grand Suite, spanning more than 1,000 square feet and located forward on Deck 6, costs a whopping $132,600 per voyage.
The Aman Suite, which is the signature suite onboard Amangati, is a spectacular living space of almost 4,000 square feet, complete with its own massage room and a huge terrace with a private jacuzzi. The most expansive accommodation option is the Premier two-bedroom suite that brings together the Aman Suite and an adjoining Premier Suite. Pricing for each of these opulent options is only available upon request.
Toward the end of March 2028, Amangati will depart Saint Jonh’s and embark on its second Atlantic Passage, an 11-night journey ending in Madeira, on March 31 2028.

2028 BMW M5 LCI Spied, Can’t Hide Neue Klasse Design Beneath the Trippy Vinyl Stickers
25 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
It’s not only the BMW 5 Series that’s getting a mid-cycle refresh, but also the range-topping series of the lineup, the G9X M5, which is currently two years old.
Usually, facelifted models stand out from their predecessors by featuring new front and rear bumpers, some tweaked lighting units at both ends, a few updates on the inside, and sometimes some modest changes beneath the skin. As a result, the average Joe can easily mistake them from their previous iterations, but there will be no such thing when it comes to the upcoming M5.
As you likely already know, because this model has been spied testing in the open numerous times these past few months, with the scoops being joined by the occasional realistic rendering that allows us to see what is new more easily, the facelifted BMW M5 won’t look anything like its predecessor. And this applies not only to the exterior, but also to the cockpit, because it has ventured into the Neue Klasse realm.
Therefore, it looks more similar to other Neue Klasse models, like the new 3 Series, the i3, iX3, and X5 than it does to outgoing M5. After all, it will feature a vizor-like face, with a pair of tiny kidney grilles being flanked by the new headlights. And speaking of the latter, the latest scooped prototype, which recently ended up in our inboxes after being immortalized by our spy photographers, appears to feature the final production headlights.
Photo: SH Proshots The front bumper is also new, and it looks a bit more aggressive. The hood and front fenders are also new, whereas the profile carries over. Out back, the facelifted BMW M5 will feature new taillights, a different bumper, and a new diffuser. Other changes will likely include new wheels, and probably some fresh colors added to the palette. Speaking of the latter, the latest spied tester had a red paint finish and sat on black alloys.
Our man with the cam could not get close enough to this prototype to take a few shots of the cockpit. However, if you zoom in through the side windows on certain pictures shared in the gallery above, then you will see a glimpse of the interior. And as you already knew, it is also part of the Neue Klasse family, just like the exterior.
Stuff such as the Panoramic iDrive, which is the brand’s pillar-to-pillar display that stretches across the entire width of the new dashboard panel at the bottom of the windshield, is on deck, and so is a new infotainment system, and likely a new steering wheel. The trim and upholstery will likely be revised, too, as part of the model’s mid-cycle refresh.
By the way, due to the serious changes inside and out, the upcoming BMW M5 could easily be mistaken for an entirely new generation, but it’s not, as what we are dealing with is a comprehensive facelift.
Photo: SH Proshots Officially, we have no idea whether a power boost is part of the makeover. The current M5 has 717 hp (535 kW/727 ps) and 738 pound-feet (1,000 Nm) of torque in total from its plug-in hybrid 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine. The M5 Sedan hits 60 mph (97 kph) in 3.4 seconds, and the M5 Touring is one-tenth of a second slower because it is a bit heavier. And in case you forgot, the modern-day M5 is also slower than its predecessor, as the electric trickery has left its toll on it.
Some believe that more oomph could indeed be part of the model’s mid-cycle refresh, and others swear it will launch with the same output and thrust. But what say you? Actually, before inviting you to scroll down to the comments box and leave your impression on the upcoming M5, we have to tell you that this vehicle will probably make its way to dealers nationwide on our shores for the 2028 model year.
After all, the current one is a 2027 model right now, and it starts at $123,300, before destination, options, and dealer fees. This is the MSRP of the BMW M5 Sedan, whereas the M5 Touring, aka the station wagon, because this one is also marketed over here, is $2,000 more expensive, as it kicks off at $125,300. Chances are the facelifted M5 will be a bit pricier than the outgoing one.
Now, what’s your take on the exterior design of the 2028 BMW M5? Do you think it looks good? Is it better than the outgoing one? What about its predecessors, namely the F90, F10 , E60, E39, and so on? To me, it looks like a cheap knockoff, and I do not fancy the interior either, because no real petrolhead wants a screen fest. Not to mention that the tech-filled cockpit will likely not age well, and chances are nobody will want this thing some ten years from now. And we cannot say the same about the older M5s, can we?

The World's First Wheel-Less Tent Trailer Brings Home-Like Comforts in the Tiniest Package
14 photos
Photo: MyGlamper
"Don't camp, glamp" says MyGlamper, the manufacturer of what is billed as the world's first wheel-less tent trailer. Designed to be super compact, very light, and incredibly versatile, the product of the same name, MyGlamper, offers a new way of camping.
That new way of camping is halfway between what you'd get with a traditional rooftop tent and a caravan/travel trailer. It's neither, but it's also a bit of both, and it came to be out of the desire to do away with the disadvantages of both solutions.
The inventor of the MyGlamper wheel-less tent trailer and the founder of the company of the same name is Gene Corbett, a man who hardly needs an introduction to Australian readers. A professional driving instructor, an awarded performance driver, and a driving safety advocate often featured in the national media, Corbett is also the Guinness record holder for the title of the Fastest Simpson Desert crossing, a feat achieved just recently in a Mahindra Scorpio in 13 hours, 21 minutes, and 5 seconds.
All these are more than just notches on a belt, impressive as they might be. They add credibility to the startup, since said startup proposes a product created, tested, and built by an experienced adventurer and true professional.
Photo: MyGlamper It also proposes a different way of camping, with a tent trailer that has no wheels. MyGlamper is actually very similar to a pop-up rooftop tent but, instead of being attached to the roof, it's hitched at the back. Corbett calls it a "trailer" but you're not towing it, since it travels upright, flat against the rear of the vehicle, so you can could still attach and pull a trailer if you wanted to.
As Corbett explains, that means you have improved aerodynamics traveling down the road with no impact on fuel consumption, but you can also bring an entire home along with you. Well, the sort of home you'd get from an inflatable canvas tent, but let's not get lost in technicalities.
MyGlamper will be available in three configurations, none of which is physically available right now. There's a Lite version that's exactly what its name implies, a basic, stripped-down, and smaller variant; there's a Plus version that's a near-complete solution, and then there's the Pro variant, which is the biggest and highest specced version.
Photo: MyGlamper We're looking at the MyGlamper Pro today, because it promises to offer sleeping for as many as 12 people "comfortably," a kitchen, a shower, and even extra stuff like a water heater and off-grid capabilities . The Pro variant doesn't even have official renders for the interior as of this writing, which probably means the manufacturer is still ironing out the final details, but if it's everything it's promoted to be, it should be a winner.
Construction is with 300 gsm RipTech Polycotton canvas for the tent part, which comes with separate chambers that inflate (and deflate) with an automatic pump.
The base, which is both the off-the-ground platform on which a double bed sits and the box that carries the entire structure during transport, is a customizable composite case. MyGlamper plans to offer options for carbon fiber construction, maybe with optional colors, later down the line.
Photo: MyGlamper The hitch that attaches the MyGlamper to your vehicle is high-quality carbon steel, and the legs and brackets are aluminum or stainless steel.
The Pro version weighs 110 kg (242 lbs) dry, and is 35 cm high, 140 cm long, and 120 cm wide (13.7 x 55 x 47 inches) in transport mode. These are the exact dimensions for the box on the back. At camp, you open the box and secure it with the provided support legs before you deploy the tent.
With the Pro, you get a bedroom on top of that elevated base and a fully-enclosed annex. Since there are no renders available for this model, it's difficult to see where MyGlamper thinks you'll be able to fit 12 beds, including the two in the bedroom, but dimensions of the entire structure come in at 225 cm in height, 460 cm in length, and 480 cm in width (88.5 x 181 x 189 inches).
Photo: MyGlamper The list of features for the Pro is impressive for a camper of this type but, again, there's no mention on where they'd have to travel, since the box will only fit the deflated, flat-packed tent structure.
That list includes includes a 30-liter (8-gallon) freshwater tank, full electrics including a heating water element, plumbings and fittings for the shower, a foldable shower base to capture and recycle water, multi-stage filtration system, self-composting Flatpack toilet, a kitchen with a 3-burner gas cooktop, queen air mattress, a power pack to charge devices and run house functions, lights, and a solar array of unspecified capabilities.
As already noted, MyGlamper is still working on the final specs list, since some of these features, like the toilet, the solar, and the kitchen, are also featured as add-ons on the same page for the product.
Photo: MyGlamper The idea is that MyGlamper wants to offer the Pro as a complete solution , whether that means for you a higher sleeping capacity or the full range of creature comforts. After all, they do say it's "designed for full-scale exploration, off-grid living, remote travel, maximum comfort."
The Pro is also designed to be "stable by design" so there won't be any need for guide ropes or tent pegs, at least according to the manufacturer. Corbett has been testing the Lite version of the MyGlamper for a long time and working on the final design for even longer – "years," he says.
Photo: MyGlamper He's also been showing off the first completed unit of the Lite at local trade events and gathering, and even offering it to fellow adventurers for independent reviews. The two videos below and some photos in the gallery show the Lite version, which doubles as a concept demonstrator.
MyGlamper Pro is now open for pre-orders, with an AUD8,997 (US$6,300) deposit locking you in for a Founders' Limited Price of AUD29,990 (US$21,000). Once the Pro reaches production, it will retail for AUD35,245 (US$24,800) before options. There is no delivery timeline for this version.

ABT's Audi RS 5 Avant Is Here With More Power and Enhanced Look
15 photos
Photo: ABT Sportsline
Having left its mark recently on quite a few models, including the Audi RS 3, RS Q8, and RS 7, to name but some, ABT Sportsline is now back under the limelight with an entirely new project called the RS5-R.
As we told you in the title, and as its name implies, it is based on the new generation Audi RS 5, which definitely does not lack in the power department. However, the tuner decided to boost its oomph to new impressive levels, so this machine now has more power than numerous previous-generation supercars. And we are still talking about a premium compact model with a five-door body style in this case, because the pictured ride is an Avant, and that is Audi slang for station wagon.
According to ABT Sportsline, this Audi RS 5 Avant benefits from the ABT Power S performance upgrade, which is said to be compatible with the myABT app, and it boasts a jaw-dropping amount of power. The output now stands at 710 brake horsepower, which equals 529 kilowatts and 720 metric horsepower, and the peak thrust is now officially rated at 667 pound-feet (905 Nm) of torque, the tuner reveals.
We definitely want to tell you just how fast the new ABT RS5-R is, but the truth is that we do not know, because the company hasn’t released this information at the time of writing. What we can remind you instead is that the standard Audi RS 5 comes with 503 hp (375 kW/510 ps) with zero outside intervention, and has 443 lb-ft (600 Nm) of torque on tap.
Photo: ABT Sportsline Power is supplied by a V6 with twin turbocharging, which has a 2.9-liter displacement, and that is how much the ICE produces. An electric motor assists it, and generates 174 hp (130 kW/177 ps) and 339 lb-ft (460 Nm) of torque. The total output stands at 630 hp (470 kW/639 ps) and the maximum torque is 608 lb-ft (825 Nm).
As a result, the ABT RS5-R is 80 hp (81 ps/60 kW) and 59 lb-ft (80 Nm) of torque more powerful than the standard Audi RS 5, which requires 3.6 seconds to complete the 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) acceleration. With the battery, which has a 22 kWh net capacity and sits under the trunk floor, fully charged, the model, which also features quattro all-wheel drive, dynamic torque vectoring, and electromechanical torque vectoring transaxle, has a 50-mile (80 km) or so range on electric power alone.
In addition to the power boost, the tuned Audi RS 5 from ABT Sportsline also benefits from a new splitter at the front with blades, new door mirror casings, side skirts, louvered front fenders, a unique wing at the rear with aero blades, and a dedicated diffuser. All the extras on the outside have been made of carbon fiber, and are available in glossy or dry carbon.
ABT Sportsline also mentions the Dinamica surfaces on the inside, as well as the carbon fiber paddle shifters behind the steering wheel, a “1 of 130” badge that sits on the center console, exclusive floor mats, bespoke door sills that further reveal the special nature of this model, ABT door sill lighting, and key covers, and the latter basically round off the makeover.
Photo: ABT Sportsline Actually, they round if off when it comes to the interior, because the ABT RS5-R also benefits from ABT sports anti-roll bars and suspension springs for a much sportier setup. The car also sits on new 22-inch forged alloys in glossy black, when it comes to the pictured example, and the alloys are called the ABT EVO Performance.
Now, as you already know from the “1 of 130” badge on the center console mentioned above, the ABT RS5-R is capped at 130 units. At this point, you are probably curious how much the conversion costs, and the entire package will set you back 65,000 euros (equal to $72,490) in Germany, including VAT, and excluding the assembly and painting costs, which are another 7,600 euros ($8,475), and the TUV inspection, which is 523.60 euros ($584).
These prices obviously exclude the base price of the car , which kicks off at 106,200 euros ($118,440) for the RS 5 Sedan in its homeland of Germany, and 107,750 euros ($120,170) for the more practical RS 5 Avant. Pricing for the US market hasn’t been announced yet, but the new RS 5 will officially touch down on our shores sometime in 2027. And it will only be the four-door model that will arrive over here, because the five-door (Avant) hasn’t been confirmed for USA.
ABT Sportsline is already preparing another round of updates for the new-gen RS 5 family, which will also include an even more serious power boost, unlocking 800 ps (789 hp/588 kW). And this one appears to be due sometime in 2027. Do you dig the ABT RS5-R?

Celebrating Five Iconic Cars That Went Into Production Half a Century Ago
16 photos
Photo: Collecting Cars
Half a century seems like a long time and indeed it is, especially in the automotive industry where things have evolved dramatically since 1976. Nevertheless, a few cars that went into production back then have managed to remain fascinating fifty years later.
The mid-1970s was a period of monumental transition, particularly in the automotive sector where manufacturers were forced to adapt to new emissions and safety regulations.
The era of unchecked performance that gave us muscle cars was over and brands were now focused on delivering either economical models, or packaging excitement in safer, more fuel-efficient models.
Despite the restrictions of the era, the mid-1970s saw the introduction of many memorable production cars that not only met but exceeded expectations and became iconic.
Bellow, we’re going to remember and celebrate five 1970s icons that, despite turning fifty this year, continue to command admiration and inspire enthusiasts as well as the industry.
Volkswagen Golf GTI Mk I Photo: Collectiong Cars Initially launched in 1974, the Golf received the gargantuan responsibility of gradually replacing the Type 1 “Beetle,” none other than the record-breaking model that put Volkswagen on the map.
With a simple yet modern design penned by Giorgetto Giugiaro , a wide range of options and simple, reliable engineering, the Golf showed it could successfully replace its iconic predecessor from an early stage, selling extremely well globally.
To boost the model’s popularity even further, VW decided to give buyers – particularly younger ones - something that it failed to deliver with the Beetle: a sporty, performance-oriented version.
Photo: Collectiong Cars That version was the Golf GTI, which the German carmaker unveiled at the Frankfurt Motor Show in September 1975.
Met with universal praise, the car went into production a few months later, in the summer of 1976 and, like its standard sibling, became hugely popular.
Weighing about 1,785 pounds (810 kg), the GTI initially featured 1.6-liter straight-four with mechanical Bosch K-Jetronic fuel injection. Rated at 108 hp, it made the small hatchback lively and absolutely thrilling to drive, which earned it a lot of fans quickly.
Today, half a century after it went into production, the Mk1 Golf GTI remains an automotive legend, one that many historians credit for pioneering the modern hot hatch segment.
Lotus Esprit S1 Photo: Collectiong Cars Like the Golf, the second entry on our list made its public debut in the fall of 1975 featuring memorable styling by Italian automotive design legend Giorgetto Giugiaro.
The original Esprit debuted in concept form at the 1975 Paris Motor Show where it was met with excitement by the public and the press.
Developed to replace the Europa as Lotus’ new mid-engine, two-seat offering, the Esprit was a huge improvement over its predecessor, particularly in terms of styling.
Photo: Collectiong Cars When it came to the mechanical side, the Esprit was initially powered by an all-new 2.0-liter Type 907 DOHC inline-four designed in-house by Lotus.
While far from perfect, the S1 Esprit , was a thrilling lightweight sports car that demanded attention with its wedge-shaped styling and captivated enthusiasts with its sublime handling.
Those qualities were dramatically improved on subsequent Esprit series, and the model became the longest-running production car in Lotus history and one of the most successful.
The Esprit helped Lotus evolve into one of the most respected sports car builders in the world and became one of Britan’s most legendary sports cars.
Porsche 924 Photo: Collectiong Cars Often forgotten, the 914 was pretty interesting, affordable mid-engine sports car co-developed by Volkswagen and Porsche. The model was produced from 1969 to 1976 and was reasonably succesful.
However, as early as 1972, the two companies decided to build a more modern successor, the development of which was handed down to Porsche but due to the 1973 oil crisis and swift strategy shift, VW pulled out of the project.
Nevertheless, development continued and the new-age affordable sports car became the Porsche 924.
Photo: Collectiong Cars First unveiled in 1975, the 924 entered production a year later. Though it was exclusively a Porsche, the car was manufactured in Audi’s Neckarsulm plant and initially received a VW 2.0-liter inline-four engine.
Despite initial fears that it would fail, the 924 quickly became popular and the lineup was eventually expanded to include a turbocharged model as well as several memorable lightweight special editions.
Produced until the end of the 1988 model year, the 924 bowed out as a Porsche icon, with strong sales for an entry-level model and pretty extensive motorsport career.
Half a century after it entered production, the sports car remains relevant, with plenty of enthusiasts cherishing surviving examples.
BMW 6 Series E24 Photo: Collectiong Cars In 1975, BMW decided to discontinue the E9 range and in January 1976, it began producing a new flagship, grand tourer-style luxury coupe range which it christened the 6 Series.
Codenamed E24, the new 6 Series retained the luxurious feel and comfort-oriented appeal of its predecessor, but wrapped everything in an aggressive, sporty-looking body designed by the famed Paul Bracq.
Combining luxury, comfort and impressive maneuverability, the 6 Series was highly-praised from the get-go, particularly in its most potent guise, which was initially the 633CSi.
Photo: Collectiong Cars That original range-topper was powered by a 3.2-liter inline-six rated at 197 hp, but 1984, it was surpassed by the M-division-built M635CSi , featuring a 3.5-liter that made no less than 282 hp.
Manufactured until the end of the 1989 model year, the E24 6 Series was a standout model of its era, one that’s still highly revered for its timeless “shark nose” design and for pioneering a new recipe for modern grand tourers by adding thrilling maneuverability to the traditional list of GT ingredients, such as supreme comfort and high-speed cruising.
Fifty years after entering production, the E24 remains a BMW legend that made history on public roads as well as motorsport.
Lamborghini Silhouette Photo: RM Sotheby's In the early 1970s, Lamborghini expanded its range with an entry-level model dubbed Urraco , hoping to increase sales.
However, the Urraco never quite lived up to the company’s expectations, selling poorly despite its eye-catching design, crisp handling and decent mid-mounted V8.
In an attempt to make the Urraco more interesting to sports car buyers, Lamborghini developed a “new” model called Silhouette, which was heavily based on the entry-level model, but upgraded with an aggressive body kit and a more potent engine
Photo: RM Sotheby's Launched in 1976, the Silhouette was powered by a 3.0-liter version of the Lambo V8 rated at 265 hp, which undoubtably made it more thrilling to drive than the initial Urraco.
Lamborghini’s first-ever targa-top model , the Silhouette was praised by the public and the press but, like the Urraco, it failed to sell as well as the company projected.
With only 54 units produced until the end of the 1979 model year, it was in fact one of Lamborghini’s greatest flops.
Despite that, fifty years later, the aggressive-looking Silhouette has become a sought-after collector’s item due to its low production figures and its wild looks. It’s currently a rare example of a sports car that flopped during its production run, but aged like fine wine and still managed to become iconic.

The 443-foot Viking Haki Is the Newest Viking River Cruise Ship
8 photos
Photo: Viking Cruises
If you’re thinking about European travel, you shouldn’t miss the stunning river cruise experiences offered by one of the most acclaimed names in the industry, Viking Cruises. Operator of a flexible fleet of river ships, ocean ships, and expedition ships, Viking knows how to take boutique cruising to the next level.
Those passionate about Norse mythology will immediately recognize Haki as the self-proclaimed King of Sweden with a cruel fate. After defeating the Swedish army led by King Hugleik, Haki proclaimed himself King of Sweden, but his rulership was short-lived. He was killed in an act of revenge by two kinsmen of the former King, just three years later.
The legendary name of this Norse king is now also the name of the latest ship to join Viking’s fleet of river cruise ships. It was officially welcomed this week, and it will join its sister ships on several itineraries on the Rhine, Main, and Danube rivers.
Haki is 443 feet long, and its boutique cruising configuration is meant to welcome just 190 guests, attended by a 53-person crew. The Viking Longship is an award-winning design, said to combine classic Scandinavian design with innovative engineering. The spacious staterooms onboard the ships in this series are heralded as the largest suites available on European rivers , and these ships also offer the most al-fresco dining.
Viking Haki’s 95-suite configuration includes 25 standard staterooms, 22 French Balcony Staterooms, 39 Veranda Staterooms, seven Veranda Suites, and two Explorer Suites. One of the characteristics of the Viking Longship is that all staterooms features two full-size rooms with a veranda accessed from the living room, plus a French balcony in the bedroom.
Such spacious accommodation is possible mainly thanks to the ingenious asymmetric corridor layout of the Viking Longship design.
Onboard amenities include the Aquavit Terrace and Lounge, a beautiful indoor/outdoor space at the bow of the ship, specifically designed for elegant al-fresco dining. The Sun Deck offers beautiful 360-degree views and shaded seating, but also houses the ship’s solar panels and an organic herb garden.
Guests also have access to a Lounge &Bar, a restaurant, and a library. The lounge and the restaurant both have floor-to-ceiling windows and doors for expansive views. Lastly, a hybrid-engine system described as “ecologically friendly” contributes to a more comfortable, smoother onboard experience for the guests, by producing fewer vibrations.
With the delivery of the new Viking Haki, Viking is on track to complete its massive fleet expansion. By 2032, this expanded fleet will boast 114 river ships, 28 ocean ships, and 28 expedition ships. Following Viking Haki, 17 more river ships will be added to the fleet in 2028, all boasting the same innovative layout, greener propulsion, and luxury onboard services.

2026 SEMA Show • Nissan Returns to the Annual SEMA Show Featuring a 300-HP Sentra Spec-V Revival Concept, Two Z Cars
The 2027 Car of the Year Finalists Are Here. Not a Single Exciting Model Among Them!
8 photos
Photo: European Car of the Year
The journey to the 2027 European Car of the Year continues with seven vehicles that will battle each other in the grand finale, and each one has an equal shot of driving home with the much-desired crown on its head.
The jury recently revealed the seven finalists for the 2027 edition of the European Car of the Year award, and the names that have made it on the list are, in alphabetical order, the BMW iX3, Cupra Raval, Hyundai Ioniq 3, Kia EV2, Renault Twingo, Volkswagen ID. Polo, and Volvo EX60. According to the jurors, “many others deserved a place on the shortlist,” but it is these that will go to the grand finale.
As you have likely noticed, the seven rides mentioned above are all EVs, and the organization noted that these fit “ perfectly with the broader trend in the European market , ” while also mentioning the “ fuel crisis triggered by the war in Iran, ” which has “ driven an increase in the number of electric car users. ” This is the first time in the award’s 63-year history when all the finalists are electric vehicles.
However, it won’t be a first win for an EV , because in case you forgot, Renault scored the award in 2024 and 2025 with the Scenic E-Tech and the 5 E-Tech, respectively, whereas the third-generation Mercedes-Benz CLA won last year’s edition. The latter entered production in mid-2025, and it is available not only as a hybrid, but also an electric vehicle, and it shares its MMA (Mercedes-Benz Modular Architecture) with the latest GLA and GLB.
Photo: European Car of the Year In order to further trim down the list, all members of the jury will reunite at the Balocco racetrack in Italy toward the end of next month, on November 25 and 26, 2026, and they will put all seven finalists through their paces, trying to decide which of them is worthy of ending up in the final. All jurors will allocate 25 points to the finalists, and they must name a winner in each round of voting, which will get a maximum of 10 points.
The jurors can cast their votes until December 31, 2026, as that is when the grand winner will be selected, and it will be kept a secret until the end of the following week, as it will be announced at the 2027 Brussels Motor Show in Belgium on January 8, 2027, which is the same venue as the last three editions of the award.
The latest BMW iX3 entered production a little over a year ago in Hungary, and the LWB model is assembled in China. The Neue Klasse electric premium compact crossover is based on the same platform as the modern-day i3, and it is offered in several configurations worldwide.
Cupra’s Raval comes to life in Spain. It is a five-door hatchback that is pretty much a sportier and more premium version of the Volkswagen ID. Polo, as it shares the same MEB+ construction. The architecture is also used by the Skoda Epiq and VW ID. Cross.
Photo: European Car of the Year As for the Hyundai Ioniq 3 , it is assembled in Turkey, and wears the design signature of SangYup Lee, the man behind the 2010 Chevy Camaro, Bentley Bentayga (together with Luc Donckerwolke), Genesis GV80, Hyundai N Vision 74 Concept, and others. The model is a subcompact hatch based on on the same platform as the Kia EV2.
Kia’s EV2 is also on the list. It comes to life in Slovakia, features a front-motor and front-wheel drive layout, and is the successor of the Soul EV (e-Soul). The e-GMP (400V) construction is used by the Hyundai Ioniq 3, as mentioned above, as well as the Kia EV3, EV4, and EV5.
Renault’s modern-day Twingo E-Tech shares its CMF-B EV (AmpR Small) nuts and bolts with the larger 4 E-Tech and 5 E-Tech, as well as the Alpina A290, Nissan Micra, and the latest Dacia Spring. It’s made in Slovenia, and is a city car (A-Segment).
Volkswagen’s ID. Polo is the latest generation of the popular supermini, and as its name implies, it is a fully-electric vehicle. It’s made in Spain, has a front-motor and front-wheel drive layout, and is based on the same platform as the Cupra Raval and Skoda Epiq, as mentioned above.
As for the Volvo EX60 , it utilizes the company’s SPA3 construction, just like the upcoming Polestar 7. It is assembled in Sweden, and has a rear-motor and rear-wheel drive, or a dual-motor and all-wheel drive layout.
Photo: European Car of the Year These seven models will fight each other in order to win the 2027 European Car of the Year Award, and as we already told you, the winner will be announced in early January, during the 2027 Brussels Motor Show. Which of these do you think deserves the crown?

Photo: © Stevanovicigor | Dreamstime.com
By Charlotte Goldstone
30 October 2026
The US ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach face potential disruption from Sunday, as around 250 security workers, represented by the International Longshore and Warehouse Union (ILWU) Local 26, prepare for strike action amid the ongoing labour dispute.
The latest labour contract extension will expire at 5pm Pacific Time on Sunday, negotiations on an extension or new deal, between the union and employers represented by the Pacific Maritime Association (PMA), continue – no strike has yet been confirmed.
However, the impact of such action would extend well beyond the security workforce. According to the PMA, approximately 85% of all container cargo at Long Beach and 33% at Los Angeles passes through the terminals employing the affected workers.
The concern is that, as industry consultant Lars Jensen pointed out, traditionally other ILWU members will not cross picket lines, potentially bringing operations at affected terminals to a standstill.
“Hence this impacts a significant part of operations,” he added, noting there was also a risk that the disruption could spread across more operations.
The threat comes as the South California port complex is handling record volumes. LA/LB processed an average of 68,000 teu a day in September, according to Mr Jensen, meaning even a short strike could quickly create bottlenecks for landside trucking and arriving vessels.
Meanwhile, inland rail congestion is already adding pressure. CargoTrans reported that, on Monday, approximately 35,700 containers were awaiting rail transportation, including around 10,500 that had been at terminals for nine days or longer.
CargoTrans advised customers with released cargo at the ports to collect it before this Sunday evening and “allow flexibility in delivery schedules”, particularly for rail shipments.
And further logistical challenges are approaching: the Vincent Thomas Bridge is scheduled to close from 7 November for approximately 16 months, potentially lengthening drayage journeys through the port complex.
Plus there is an ‘international dockworker day of action’ today, 30 October, with the Palestinian-led BDS movement reporting that more than 25 unions across 22 countries are planning strikes, demonstrations, or other action in protest against war and militarisation.
The action, endorsed by 17 Palestinian trade unions and confederations, includes 24-hour strikes in France, Italy, India, Greece, and Turkey, alongside demonstrations and rallies at ports and in cities across four continents.
Markos Bekris, president of Greek dockworkers’ union ENEDEP, said: “Dockworkers do not work for war.”
The campaigners want an end to militarisation and military relations with Israel, citing the conflict in Gaza.
While the international campaign is separate from the ILWU Local 26’s dispute, both developments highlight the potential for labour action to affect port operations and international supply chains.
At the time of writing, negotiations at Los Angeles and Long Beach are ongoing, with no strike yet confirmed.

2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Dodge Charger Gets Special-Edition Package Celebrating 90 Years of Mopar
Lamborghini’s New Temerario Tettonero Is for Deep-Pocketed Enthusiasts
6 photos
Photo: Lamborghini
Lamborghini’s most-customizable Urus ever, the Urus SE Tettonero Capsule , which was unveiled half a year as a collaboration between Centro Stile and Ad Personam, and is capped at 630 units, now has a low-riding sibling: the Temerario Tettonero.
Just like the crossover mentioned above, the new Lamborghini Temerario Tettonero is all about extra customization, as the Raging Bull wants to render a small chunk of the tuning world useless. Whether it has done that or not is up to you to decide, though whatever your answer may be, it is hard to deny the coolness of this supercar, which is now available in more configurations than ever straight from the Sant’Agata Bolognese factory, which is where it is assembled.
According to Lamborghini , interested parties can choose between five exterior colors on the new Temerario Tettonero, which is an exclusive two-tone capsule edition developed by Centro Stile. These include the Viola Pasifae, Verde Scandal, Arancio Xanto, Verde Scandal, and Blu Cepheus. It features Nero Noctis on the roof, hood, and other components, and the contrasting accents are said to extend on the front apron that sports hexagonal motifs, and on the rear diffuser.
Moreover, the company also mentions the contrasting accents on the engine surround and Lamborghini emblem, as well as optional accents in Nero Noctis that can be applied to the front bumper and hood. The front and rear bumpers, as well as the door mirror casings and the OEM wheels sport a high gloss black look for even more contrast and extra customization, thus helping the brand’s modern-day “baby” supercar stand out more next to its regular siblings.
Photo: Lamborghini On the inside, Lamborghini’s new Temerario Tettonero benefits from Q-citura seats that sport a hexagonal pattern and can be specified with match-to-body contrast stitching as an option. The Nero Ade upholstery is joined by the Grigio Octans contrast stitching. Each headrest benefits from the embroidered Lamborghini logo, and the Tettonero lettering is embroidered on the door cards.
Contributing to the supercars enhanced nature is an embroidered two-tone silhouette of the rear design on the bulkhead in color-matched stitching, and the thing that pretty much rounds things up is the dedicated limited edition plaque on the driver’s side in matte carbon, which identifies each car within the limited series.
Yep, just like the Urus SE Tettonero, the Lamborghini Temerario Tettonero will also be offered in limited numbers, and if you are curious about how many of them will see the light of day, then so are we, because the company hasn’t released this aspect at the time of writing. Needless to say that everything adds up to a pretty sum that makes the model even more expensive.
And that’s not exactly a surprise, given that the regular Lamborghini Temerario kicks off at just under $400,000 before destination and options, and it is not uncommon for certain examples to cost more than half a million dollars new.
By the way, the Tettonero factory makeover does not include a power boost, but you already knew that, didn’t you? And to be honest, it is not like the Lamborghini Temerario needs more oomph in order to stand out more, as it is already extremely powerful to the point where it makes its predecessors, the Huracan and the Gallardo, look like children’s toys.
Photo: Lamborghini The model packs a V8 engine instead of a naturally aspirated V10, and the mill features twin turbocharging. It has a 4.0-liter displacement, and three electric motors assist it. Thus, the Temerario is a plug-in hybrid supercar, one that has no fewer than 902 hp (677 kW/920 ps) combined, with 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) at 9,000-9,750 rpm and 530 lb-ft (730 Nm) of torque available between 4,000 and 7,000 rpm being produced by the internal combustion engine.
The all-wheel drive supercar can keep pushing all the way up to 213 mph (343 kph), the spec sheet reveals, and takes just 2.7 seconds to sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph). This makes it two-tenths of a second slower than the punchier, larger, and pricier Revuelto, and three-tenths of a second slower than the new Revuelto SuperVeloce (SV).
As a reminder, the Lamborghini Temerario entered production in 2025, and lent its nuts and bolts to the Audi Nuvolari. So far, the company offers it as a two-door coupe, but a two-door convertible, which will add the Spyder moniker, is in development as we speak. It has been spied testing on several occasions with its power-retractable roof that that takes around 17 seconds to lower or raise, and it should be a hair slower than its fixed-roof sibling, given that it will be a bit heavier.
Given that it is not exactly convertible season in the northern hemisphere, we expect the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder to reach dealerships worldwide, including in North America, sometime next summer, with the official unveiling likely taking place a few months from now.

Setara Biosciences has formed around a handful of assets from Actio Biosciences, which was acquired by Jazz Pharmaceuticals earlier this year.
After buying Actio Biosciences earlier this year, Jazz Pharmaceuticals had some rare disease assets to spare. And so, Setara Biosciences has been formed with $90 million in series A funds to work on the remaining small molecule precision medicine programs.
Setara broke cover Friday with the fundraising announcement, led by the founder of Actio, human genetics expert David Goldstein. He will serve as president and executive officer of the new biotech.
“We are incredibly proud of what we built at Actio and that ABS-1230 for KCNT1-related epilepsy now has the opportunity to advance as part of Jazz,” Goldstein said in a statement. “Setara allows us to take the next step in our journey, to carry forward a pipeline of promising programs for rare diseases, with the potential to ultimately reach much broader patient populations.”
Jazz bought Actio for its lead program ABS-1230, which is being developed for KCNT1-related epilepsy. The deal offered up to $1.3 billion, including $820 million in upfront cash. At the time, Jazz promised to spin out the remaining assets and retain a stake in the resulting venture.
The lead asset for Setara will be the TRPV4 inhibitor STAR-0871, previously known as ABS-0871, which is under development for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2C (CMT2C) and overactive bladder. CMT2C is a rare genetic neuropathy that causes vocal cord anomalies, impairment of respiratory muscles, hearing loss and weakness in the hands and feet.
Venture capital
Alphabet’s GV is one of biotech’s most influential corporate investors
The corporate investor arms of Eli Lilly, Sanofi and Pfizer have participated in billions worth of venture capital rounds, but GV is the industry’s biggest spender.
October 27, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Annalee Armstrong
Read more
The therapy, which aims to address the underlying cause of the disease, has already gone through a Phase 1 trial in healthy volunteers. A Phase 1b study in patients with CMT2C will get underway in 2027. The therapy already has rare pediatric disease, orphan drug and fast track designations from the FDA.
But Setara hopes that STAR-0871 will have some application in more common conditions, including overactive bladder. The company will kick off a Phase 2a study in this indication at the same time.
Setara has also snagged some earlier-stage programs from Actio focused on genetic epilepsies and expansion indications, including migraine. Participating in the series A were Deerfield Management, Canaan, Droia Ventures, EcoR1, Euclidean Capital, Regeneron Ventures and Jazz.

Venti Technologies’ driverless container trucks have worked PSA’s port in Singapore for nearly three years. Traffic there runs in one big loop, so the trucks never had to back up.
U.S. rail yards are less forgiving. Venti says a Class I intermodal railroad plans to run more than 130 Venti trucks across eight sites by 2027. First, the Boston-based company had to teach its trucks two skills Singapore never required, founder and CEO Heidi Wyle told FreightWaves.
Backing an articulated rig is among trucking’s most challenging maneuvers, FreightWaves noted when Outrider added autonomous trailer backing to its distribution-yard tractors in 2022.
“So now when we came to the US, we had to teach our big 60-foot-long tractor-trailer vehicles how to back up,” Wyle said. “So you know we have videos of them actually backing up with 4-inch clearance on either side.”
Where the trucks fit in an intermodal yard
At an intermodal terminal, hostlers bring containers trackside or to the storage area . That trackside shuttle is the work the railroad wants Venti’s trucks to take on, Wyle said. She put monthly driver turnover in some places at around 20%.
“If you ask where is it that people don’t want to be, it’s in Texas in July, right?” Wyle said. “So basically what they want us to do is to be trackside with the trains and have the vehicles do the unloading and the short hauls to get to the long hauls or the other wherever else they’re going to go.”
The company’s Oct. 1 r el ease says the trucks will load, move, and unload containers during live yard operations with nobody in the cab and no dedicated lanes. It does not say whether human hostlers will keep working beside them at the U.S. sites.
The trucks also have to cross live track on their own.
“Our vehicle now sees trains,” Wyle said. “It’s just like you or I. They would see trains, you know, they would see the sign come down. We see lights, red lights, green lights just like humans do.”
Six weeks into a three-month pilot
The railroad deal grew out of a proof of concept scheduled for three months, Wyle said. Six weeks in, the railroad told Venti it had hit all the metrics. It then took two vehicles before committing to a larger rollout.
Venti signed a long-term agreement with the railroad in July, starting at two of its busiest U.S. intermodal facilities, according to the company’s July 8 release . That release projected “100-plus” trucks by 2027. The October release raised the figure to more than 130 and said the fleet could pass 600 by the end of the decade.
But the U.S. fleet has not started work. Neither company has named the railroad or disclosed terms. Venti announced a $28.8 million Series A in March 2023, led by LG Technology Ventures.
Nearly three years without a driver in Singapore
Wyle co-founded Venti in 2018 with Daniela Rus, director of MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. Their first idea was slow-speed robotaxis for senior communities. Wyle dropped it quickly.
“That was a very bad market because they don’t have a lot of money and what they have they don’t want to part with,” she said.
PSA, which runs over 70 deepsea, rail, and inland terminals according to its January release , pulled Venti into logistics around 2020, Wyle said. The two mapped PSA’s Singapore port and developed the system there, and the fleet grew from one truck to two, four, and eight. Venti now runs a 30-truck driverless fleet in Asia, Wyle said.
At PSA Singapore, those trucks work beside about 1,200 human-driven trucks, according to the Oct. 1 release. The company says its fleet has logged more than 500,000 autonomous miles and moved more than 360,000 containers.
Rebuilding the intermodal yard
The larger payoff, Wyle said, is predictability. In intermodal yards today, chassis get dropped wherever there is room, and owners sometimes send drones to find them, she said.
“What’s interesting is when you think about it for a minute, autonomy, our trucks are going to be exactly at a place exactly when they’re supposed to be there,” she said. “And so it enables a complete redo of all of those yards and the core supply chain.”
The railroad wants to start that work, she said.
“One of the things they want to do is actually start rebuilding the supply chain yards so that they’re less chaotic and more controlled,” Wyle said.
Why it matters: Venti’s trucks have run without drivers in Singapore for nearly three years. The company is now moving to test this technology in US yards, part of a growing group of autonomous technology providers targeting areas outside of middle mile and long haul applications.

The Second Orient Express Sailing Yacht to Debut in 2027 with a Mediterranean Voyage
8 photos
Photo: Orient Express Sailing Yachts
The first-ever cruise ship operating under the famous Orient Express brand was also launched as the world’s biggest luxury sailing yacht. Orient Express Corinthian has kicked off its maiden season earlier this year, and will be joined by its almost-identical sister ship, Orient Express Olympian, as soon as next year.
In the summer of 2025, Accor Cruises was confirming that a second Orient Express sailing yacht was already under construction. The second ship was names Olympian and its steel-cutting ceremony at the beginning of last year was actually said to have been celebrated at the same time as Corinthian’s keel-laying ceremony. In other words, the Group who owns the Orient Express brand moved fast to get both ships out on the water as soon as possible.
Plus, it was rumored that the deal with Chantiers de l'Atlantique, the acclaimed French shipyard that was tapped for the construction of these two luxury yachts, included an option for two more yachts, all identical. However, no new Orient Express yachts, beyond Corinthian and Olympian, have been officially confirmed so far.
O.E. Olympian is ready to make its debut next year, just one year after Corinthian , as the luxury operator has already introduced the first itineraries of the new yacht, available for booking. It looks like Olympian will first embark on a charming Mediterranean voyage from Portofino to Corsica, suggestively entitled “Mediterranean Blooms”. The four-night trip will start on May 23, and prices per suite start at an intimidating €24,200 ($27.100).
It's no surprise that the Orient Express brand expansion to the world of luxury cruising will come with steep prices for guests. Beyond the Orient Express heritage itself, these ships look and feel like floating museums, boasting spectacular interior design inspired by the Orient Express era, coupled with the latest amenities in the ultra-luxury niche.
Both Corinthian and Olympian are also innovators in terms of sailing technology and clean propulsion. They are based on the original Silenseas ship concept and SolidSail technology, both by the Chantiers de l’Atlantique, were they were actually built. The concept combines wind-power propulsion with a hybrid engine that allows an extended range.
The engine is a dual-fuel Wartsila model compatible with LNG (liquid natural gas). Norwegian company Brunvoll has developed custom propellers specifically for these sailing ships, in collaboration with the shipyard.
Both ships were also equipped with dynamic positioning that eliminates anchoring, and an AI-driven detection system that prevents the risk of marine mammal collision. Both of these features help to minimize the overall impact on marine wildlife. Last but not least, the onboard systems also include more than 6,000 sensors that monitor every energy source onboard, to maximize efficiency.
At 721-feet (220) meters, Orient Express Corinthian and Olympian are also heralded as the world’s biggest sailing yachts.
